name: Repetitive Phrase & Crutch Detection
description: Analyzes the text for the over-reliance on specific, multi-word transitional phrases, introductory clauses, and semantic crutches. AI models, trained heavily on standard essay formats and safety guidelines, develop a structural dependency on certain phrases to buffer their statements, transition between paragraphs, or maintain a neutral tone (e.g., 'It is important to note that...', 'Ultimately...', 'Furthermore...', 'As a result...'). Humans naturally use a much wider, more organic variety of transitions and phrasing.
algorithm: Transitional Phrase Profiling and Lexical Crutch Matching
mechanism: The algorithm scans the document against a dynamic database of known AI 'crutch' phrases and transitional markers. It calculates the frequency of these multi-word expressions relative to the total word count. The system specifically looks at paragraph boundaries—where AI models are notoriously prone to using rigid transitional phrases ('In conclusion', 'On the other hand'). A 'Phrase Repetition Score' is generated by measuring both the raw count of these specific clichés and the lack of variation when transitioning between ideas (e.g., using 'Moreover' three times in a single essay).
useCase: Highly effective for reviewing student essays, standard marketing copy, and informative articles where prompt constraints often force the AI into rigid, algorithmic paragraph structures.
strengths:
• Exceptional at catching 'lazy' zero-shot generation where the AI falls back on its most highly weighted, generic transitional structures.
• Provides highly interpretable results; flagging specific repeated phrases is easy for human auditors to verify.
limitations:
• Susceptible to prompt engineering (e.g., 'Do not use phrases like "In conclusion"').
• May penalize human writers who correspond in highly templated corporate speak or beginner writers who strictly follow rigid academic essay formulas.
parameters:
Analysis: Multi-word Expression and Transitional Marker Matching
Metric: Crutch Phrase Density and Transition Variance
Output: 0-100 Phrase Repetition (Template Dependency) Score
accuracy: Moderate — 65-75% accuracy. Operates best as an immediate red-flag indicator, but requires confirmation from deeper probabilistic methods (like Log-Likelihood Rank) due to potential human overlap.

references.title: Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
